Yes—very likely.

At **37.4° above the southwestern horizon** (azimuth **217°**, roughly southwest), the Moon is comfortably high and unobstructed by normal horizon haze. With **25.9% illumination**, it is a substantial waxing crescent, not an extremely thin or difficult one.

Although astronomical twilight has not quite ended—the Sun is **13.5° below the horizon**—the sky should already be dark enough for such a crescent to stand out clearly in **clear conditions**. Its **61° separation from the Sun** also makes it easy to distinguish from the brighter twilight region.

Look **southwest**, about **four fist-widths above the horizon** at arm’s length. Assuming buildings or clouds do not block that direction, you should be able to see it readily with unaided eyes. Cairo’s light pollution should not prevent seeing a Moon this bright.
